# hackbot

A Go-first bot with Python helpers, by [@rjwashi](https://github.com/rjwashi).

**Design:** Go owns the core bot logic (config, loop, I/O, analysis). Anything Go
can't do cleanly is delegated to small, self-contained Python helpers under
`pythontools/`, invoked via `exec.Command`.

## Layout

Every file and directory, as full paths (directories end with `/`). This block
is generated from the working tree with `hackbot layout`; a test fails if it
drifts, so regenerate it whenever you add a file or directory.

## Requirements

- [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) 1.27+
- Python 3.11+ (only needed for `hackbot py ...`)
- [nmap](https://nmap.org/download.html) (only needed for `hackbot nmap scan ...`)
- [vulscan](https://github.com/scipag/vulscan) (optional; only for `-vulscan`)

## Build & run

```bash
go build -o bin/hackbot.exe .
./bin/hackbot.exe hello
./bin/hackbot.exe run
./bin/hackbot.exe version
```

### Python helpers

```bash
./bin/hackbot.exe py helpers.py slugify "Hello World"   # -> hello-world
```

## Agents

hackbot ships a set of composable security **agents** (full catalog and
recommendations in [`docs/agents.md`](docs/agents.md)). Run `hackbot agents` to
print them. The registry in `main.go` is the single source of truth; the table
in the docs and the snapshot below are generated from it and kept honest by a
test. Every agent is designed to become an OpenCode **skill** later
(`hackbot agents -format skill -name <agent>`).

### Web Security Testing (WSTG)

Twelve agents cover the OWASP Web Security Testing Guide, one per checklist
under `src/agent_files/` (parsed by `internal/wstg` and embedded into the binary).
Use `web list` to see them and `web show <category>` to print a category's tests:

```bash
hackbot web list                 # all 12 categories and their test counts
hackbot web show injection       # the WSTG-INJT checklist
hackbot web show WSTG-APIT       # code, name, or file name also work
hackbot web list -json           # machine-readable
```

Each checklist is treated as the agent's **capability list**. A curated layer
maps tests to free/open-source tools (`web tools`) and shows, per test, either a
runnable command or manual guidance (`web plan`). Tests that cannot be automated
safely stay manual on purpose:

```bash
hackbot web tools                # the free/open-source tool catalog
hackbot web tools injection      # tools for one category
hackbot web plan injection       # every test -> tool command or manual guidance
hackbot web run injection 10.0.0.1 -test WSTG-INJT-05   # guarded (dry-run default)
```

`web run` is **dry-run by default** and only touches the network when scanning is
enabled *and* the target is allowlisted (same gates as nmap). Argument templates
are fixed, so target input is never shell-interpolated.

## Recon / OSINT agent (`recon`)

The `recon` family runs free/open-source reconnaissance tools against an
allowlisted domain or host. Each task is a capability backed by one tool:

```bash
hackbot recon list               # the tasks (subdomains, dns, ports, ...)
hackbot recon chains             # the pipelines (currently: footprint)
hackbot recon tools              # free tool catalog (subfinder, dnsx, naabu, ...)
hackbot recon tools subdomains   # alternates for one task
hackbot recon plan               # every task and the exact command it runs
hackbot recon subdomains example.com   # guarded (dry-run by default)
hackbot recon footprint example.com    # chain: subdomains -> live HTTP
```

Tasks: `subdomains` (subfinder), `dns` (dnsx), `ports` (naabu), `services`
(nmap), `http` (httpx), `whois`, `urls` (gau).

Chains wire one task's output into the next without any shell, so there is no
command injection through target-derived data. `recon footprint` runs subfinder
and pipes the discovered subdomains straight into httpx via a real stdin pipe
(`ops.RunChain` + `scan.StdinRunner`). A chain is gated once, up front, with the
same `enable_scan` + `allowed_*` rules as a single task, and it stops at the first
failing step instead of feeding empty input to the rest.

## Content discovery agent (`discover`)

The `discover` family brute-forces web content with ffuf/gobuster against an
allowlisted target, using a wordlist from `wordlist`/`-wordlist` (defaults to the
free SecLists `common.txt`):

```bash
hackbot discover list
hackbot discover tools
hackbot discover plan
hackbot discover dirs example.com         # guarded (dry-run by default)
hackbot discover vhosts 10.0.0.5 -wordlist /path/to/list.txt
```

Tasks: `dirs`, `files`, `extensions`, `vhosts`, `params`.

Both families share the guarded runner in `internal/ops`: dry-run unless
`-dry-run=false`, and real runs require `enable_scan=true` plus a target inside
`allowed_targets` (IP/CIDR) or `allowed_domains` (name).

## Secret-scanning agent (`secrets`)

The `secrets` family scans a **local path** (a checkout or a git repository) for
leaked credentials with free scanners. It is a *path* catalog: the gate is
`enable_scan=true` plus the path being inside `allowed_paths`, not the network
allowlists, because the target is a directory rather than a host:

```bash
hackbot secrets list
hackbot secrets tools
hackbot secrets plan
hackbot secrets scan .            # working tree (gitleaks); guarded, dry-run default
hackbot secrets history .         # full git history (gitleaks)
hackbot secrets verify .          # only live-verified findings (trufflehog)
hackbot secrets entropy .         # entropy/pattern baseline (detect-secrets)
```

Tasks: `scan` and `history` (gitleaks), `verify` (trufflehog), `entropy`
(detect-secrets). All read local files only; `verify` may contact the issuing
service to confirm a credential is live.

## Dependency / SBOM agent (`deps`)

The `deps` family produces a software bill of materials and a vulnerability
report for a local project, also gated by `allowed_paths`:

```bash
hackbot deps list
hackbot deps tools
hackbot deps plan
hackbot deps vulns .              # dependency + OS CVE scan (trivy)
hackbot deps sbom .               # CycloneDX SBOM (syft)
hackbot deps grype .              # alternate DB match (grype)
hackbot deps osv .                # OSV database scan (osv-scanner)
```

Tasks: `vulns` (trivy), `sbom` (syft), `grype` (grype), `osv` (osv-scanner).
These tools download their vulnerability databases, so "local" means the scanned
files are local; the database updates make outbound requests.

## nmap agent

hackbot can ingest nmap results and run a modular analysis pipeline:

```
parse -> rule-based risk report -> [LLM explanation] -> [GitHub issues]
```

### Commands

```bash
# Parse an nmap XML file and list hosts/ports
hackbot nmap parse   scan.xml

# Rule-based risk report (flags risky exposed services)
hackbot nmap analyze scan.xml

# NSE script (recon) output: banners, page titles, headers, keys
hackbot nmap recon   scan.xml

# vulscan (VulDB) vulnerability matches from NSE output
hackbot nmap vulscan scan.xml

# GUARDED scan of an allowlisted target, then analyze + recon
hackbot nmap scan    192.168.1.10

# GUARDED scan with vulscan added
hackbot nmap scan    192.168.1.10 -vulscan

# CVE search by category / keyword / detected software
hackbot cve search xss
hackbot cve keyword "redis 7.0"
hackbot cve scan scan.xml

# List every agent
hackbot agents

# Web Security Testing (WSTG) checklists
hackbot web list
hackbot web show injection

# Full pipeline (flags work anywhere on the line)
hackbot nmap pipeline scan.xml -llm -issues -repo rjwashi/hackbot -min-severity high

# Add -json to any nmap command for machine-readable output
hackbot nmap analyze scan.xml -json
```

Produce the XML input with nmap yourself:

```bash
nmap -sV -oX scan.xml 192.168.1.0/24
```

### Risk rules

`internal/nmap` flags commonly-sensitive exposed services (Docker API, Redis,
MongoDB, SMB, RDP, databases, …) with a severity, and lists other open ports as
`INFO`. It is conservative: it reports *exposure*, not a confirmed vulnerability.

### NSE recon

hackbot parses Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE) output from XML and can run a safe
recon profile during guarded scans. Ingestion works on any XML containing
`<script>` output (per-port or host-level `<hostscript>`):

```bash
hackbot nmap recon scan.xml          # list script results
hackbot nmap recon scan.xml -json    # machine-readable
```

When scanning, a conservative default profile runs
(`banner`, `http-title`, `http-headers`, `ssh-hostkey`, `ssl-cert`). Override it
with `-scripts`, or disable it with `-scripts none`:

```bash
hackbot nmap scan 192.168.1.10 -scripts safe,default   # nmap categories work too
hackbot nmap scan 192.168.1.10 -scripts none           # ports/services only
hackbot nmap scan 192.168.1.10 -script-args http.useragent=hackbot
```

NSE output is also folded into the pipeline report (`nmap pipeline`) and the LLM
prompt.

### vulscan recon

[scipag/vulscan](https://github.com/scipag/vulscan) is an NSE script that
matches fingerprinted services against offline VulDB databases and prints
`[id] title` rows. hackbot parses those rows and reports them as **potential**
(not confirmed) findings at `MEDIUM`:

```bash
hackbot nmap vulscan scan.xml          # human summary
hackbot nmap vulscan scan.xml -json    # machine-readable
```

Install vulscan into nmap's scripts dir (documented install) and add it to a
guarded scan with `-vulscan`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/scipag/vulscan /usr/share/nmap/scripts/vulscan
hackbot nmap scan 192.168.1.10 -vulscan
```

Point at a custom checkout or a single database via config/env:

```bash
HACKBOT_VULSCAN_DIR=/opt/vulscan HACKBOT_VULSCAN_DB=cve.csv \
  hackbot nmap scan 192.168.1.10 -vulscan
```

### LLM stage

Set an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. OpenCode Zen) and `-llm` will ask the
model to prioritize findings and suggest remediation:

```bash
export HACKBOT_LLM_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/v1
export HACKBOT_LLM_API_KEY=...
export HACKBOT_LLM_MODEL=step-5-preview-free
hackbot nmap pipeline scan.xml -llm
```

If the LLM isn't configured, the stage is skipped with a note (no error).

### Actions stage

`-issues` files one GitHub issue per finding at or above `-min-severity`
(default `high`), capped by `-max-issues` (default 10). **Issue creation is
dry-run by default**; pass `-dry-run=false` to actually create issues via `gh`.
Findings can also just be exported with `-json` for your own tooling.

## CVE search (NVD) agent

Search public vulnerability data by category, keyword, or the software nmap
detected. Defaults to the free NIST
[NVD 2.0 API](https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities) (read-only); no
key is required.

```bash
hackbot cve categories                 # list categories (xss, sqli, rce, ...)
hackbot cve search xss                 # CVEs for a category, worst-first
hackbot cve search rce -limit 10 -min-score 7
hackbot cve keyword "apache 2.4"       # free-text search
hackbot cve scan scan.xml              # CVEs for nmap-detected software
```

Set `nvd_api_key` (`HACKBOT_NVD_API_KEY`) to raise the NVD rate limit from
5 to 50 requests / 30s. `nvd_base_url` overrides the endpoint (mirrors/tests).

See [`docs/agents.md`](docs/agents.md) for the full agent list and
recommendations on gathering richer reports (EPSS, CISA KEV, OSV/GHSA,
CPE-based matching, caching, SARIF/CycloneDX).

## ⚠️ Authorized use only

Scanning networks you do not own or lack written permission to test is illegal
in many jurisdictions. hackbot enforces a hard safety model:

1. **Scanning is disabled by default.** It requires `enable_scan=true`
   (or `HACKBOT_ENABLE_SCAN=1`).
2. **Allowlist required.** A target is only scanned if it is inside
   `allowed_targets` (an IP or CIDR) **or** `allowed_domains` (a domain, whose
   subdomains are also in scope). Local scanners (`secrets`, `deps`) instead
   require the path to be inside `allowed_paths` (with no roots configured, the
   current working directory is the only allowed root). Out-of-scope targets are
   refused before any tool is invoked. The recon/discovery/`web run` agents share
   this model, and it is enforced by one shared gate (`ops.CheckScope`).
3. **Dry-run is the default for actions.** `web run`, `recon *`, `discover *`,
   `secrets *`, `deps *`, and GitHub issue creation send nothing until you pass
   `-dry-run=false`.
4. **Ingestion is the default mode.** Use `nmap parse`/`analyze`/`pipeline` on
   XML you produced yourself; no scanning happens.

Only scan systems you own or are explicitly authorized to test.

## Configuration

Optional JSON file (`-config hackbot.json`, see `hackbot.example.json`) with
env-var overrides:

| File key | Env var | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `HACKBOT_NAME` | `hackbot` | display name |
| `interval_seconds` | `HACKBOT_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `60` | bot loop tick |
| `python_cmd` | `HACKBOT_PYTHON_CMD` | `python` | interpreter for helpers |
| `enable_scan` | `HACKBOT_ENABLE_SCAN` | `false` | master scan switch |
| `allowed_targets` | `HACKBOT_ALLOWED_TARGETS` | _(empty)_ | comma-separated IPs/CIDRs |
| `allowed_domains` | `HACKBOT_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` | _(empty)_ | comma-separated domains (recon/discover); subdomains allowed |
| `allowed_paths` | `HACKBOT_ALLOWED_PATHS` | _(empty)_ | comma-separated local dirs for `secrets`/`deps`; empty means the cwd |
| `wordlist` | `HACKBOT_WORDLIST` | SecLists `common.txt` | wordlist for content discovery |
| `nmap_path` | `HACKBOT_NMAP_PATH` | `nmap` | nmap binary |
| `nmap_scripts` | `HACKBOT_NMAP_SCRIPTS` | _(safe recon set)_ | comma-separated NSE scripts; `none` disables |
| `nmap_script_args` | `HACKBOT_NMAP_SCRIPT_ARGS` | _(empty)_ | extra nmap `--script-args` |
| `vulscan_dir` | `HACKBOT_VULSCAN_DIR` | _(empty)_ | vulscan checkout dir |
| `vulscan_db` | `HACKBOT_VULSCAN_DB` | _(empty)_ | vulscan database name |
| `llm_base_url` | `HACKBOT_LLM_BASE_URL` | _(empty)_ | OpenAI-compatible base URL |
| `llm_api_key` | `HACKBOT_LLM_API_KEY` | _(empty)_ | LLM auth token |
| `llm_model` | `HACKBOT_LLM_MODEL` | _(empty)_ | model ID |
| `github_repo` | `HACKBOT_GITHUB_REPO` | _(empty)_ | `owner/name` for issues |
| `nvd_base_url` | `HACKBOT_NVD_BASE_URL` | NVD 2.0 endpoint | CVE API endpoint |
| `nvd_api_key` | `HACKBOT_NVD_API_KEY` | _(empty)_ | raises NVD rate limit |

## Testing

```bash
go test ./... -race -cover     # Go tests
python -m pytest pythontools   # Python helper tests
```

CI runs both on every push and pull request.

## Status

Early scaffold — core loop, Python escape hatch, the nmap analysis/agent
pipeline (analyze + NSE recon + vulscan), a CVE search (NVD) agent, 12 OWASP
WSTG web-security-testing agents, and guarded recon/OSINT (`recon`, with a
`footprint` chain), content discovery (`discover`), secret-scanning (`secrets`),
and dependency/SBOM (`deps`) agents are in place; broader bot features are
tracked as issues. See `docs/agents.md`.
